To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DNA–DNA attraction in the condensates is pairwise, driven by electrostatic interactions of DNA with the polycations, and not by hydration forces; that the concentration of bridged cations, not the concentration of adsorbed cation, is the main factor that determines the magnitude of the DNA– DNA interaction; and that the condensates have a high degree of orientational order, but the DNA and the cations are highly mobile.
DNA condensation is driven by electrostatic forces of polycations, not hydration, and that the DNA–DNA interaction is pairwise and mediated by bridging cations.
DNA condensation is driven by polycation-mediated electrostatics and not by hydration, and that the concentration of bridged cations determines the magnitude of the DNA– DNA force.
